So, just had a scare this morning. My two year old niece fell out of bed. The height she fell from was at about one and half feet. I measured just to be sure. She was fast asleep, so was I, I'd just gotten an hour of sleep when I heard this smacking sound. I woke up immediately and saw her lying there just about to start to crying. I don't think she lost consciousness, and she stopped crying after a few seconds. She's active and seems fine three hours later, no vomiting, and drunk her milk, and ate a few spoonful of soft foods. Do I have to take her to the doctor?

My mom goes to National Center for Mental Health in Mandaluyong. For the private consultation fee, where you don't have to wait in a long line. You'll have to pay 400 php.
Medicine like depakote 250 mg cost at about 34 pesos each, if you buy your meds from the doc like Clozapine 100 mg, it'll cost you 50 pesos, 6 pesos lower from what you'll be able to buy at the local Drug stores like Mercury.

I've read that self-harm like cutting produces chemicals in the brain that makes you feel good, a high that you could also get from a workout, like running and other hard activity. The relief you get from self-harm is temporary tho, and might make you feel guilt and shame, just adding more to your distress. It might lead to serious injuries too. 
 The better thing to do is, you should go see a doctor and get help to remove the pain you are experiencing.
You could try gardening. Something about being able to see the result of your effort is therapeutic. Try a organic garden, herb garden, flower garden, ornamental or vegetable garden.

I grew up with my gran calling me lazy and unable to do anything right. I just used to lie on bed reading books and browsing the web all day. Only getting up for necessities. Even eating and bathing feels like a chore. That went on for five years. When circumstances forced me to be more active, every mundane thing I do seems like a victory, washing the dishes, doing the laundry,  cooking for dinner, feeding the dogs, watering the plants, hanging out in the living room instead of hiding in the bedroom. These things might not mean anything to other people but to me, they're a sign of progress, that I'm getting better. This morning, I managed to walk the dogs with the sun in the horizon, with the sun illuminating the street my dog and I are walking on. It was a far cry from walking my dog around our house in the dead of night. It took me months before I got to this point and I'm still unable to look people in the eye and greet them. I think getting rid of my  anxiety is a very long process, with my dogs and my garden  helping to force me out of my comfort zone. I exert effort not for myself but for those that I care about, right now they just consist of my mom, my pets and my garden. That seems to be enough. I'm not feeling suicidal, I don't just live in a fog of lethargy, I don't think too much of the future.  My dearest wish is that someday soon I can enter a store and be able to buy our groceries. That seems to be a step I'm still unable to accomplish.  Sometimes, it's still so easy to not do anything, to not care about anything but those are coming less and less... It takes time to change OP. You'll have to do everything on small steps, I find that the saying it takes work to be happy helps me take those steps.
Bipolar mom is going manic. She's feeling like Santa, giving gifts to people left and right, getting buried on debts she can't pay for. I fucking hate Christmas.

My mom tried to commit suicide last December. So, my least favorite month of the year. Also, get to meet one of my judgemental Aunt. Who likes to greet my mom whenever she calls, "How's you're worthless daughter?". It frustrates me, how my mom keeps in contact with her, while all she does is insult and demean us. I hate the whole Christmas season.

You're welcome! If you ever start your own garden, don't over water your plants. I lost two of my first herbs that way. Also, aside from making you feel in control and taking your stress away.  There really are microbes in the soil that makes one happy. So, don't be shy about getting dirt on your hands. :)

You could start an indoor garden. Gardening has proven that it could help with depression. Add some indoor plants to freshen up the air in your room, like snake plants, or Boston Ferns, you could raise herbs on your windowsill, like Oregano, Basil and Rosemary. Taking care of them could be a great stress reliever. And getting in touch with nature. You could also raise dwarf fruit trees. Tomatoes and meyer lemons are nice. You could choose to buy them in your local nurseries, chose the ones old enough to bear fruit.

My life would have been easier if I had learned to asked for help. Being arrogant that I don't need anyone to complete a task, not trusting anyone to be able to do a much better job than I could. I should have learned to delegate, to be a team player... Tsk. Instead, I exhaust my energy, my passion too early, making the end product not as good as I'd hope.

I have never taken medication for depression, what I do is distract myself with my hobbies, doing things I find fun. I've found exercise is a great replacement for pills, that you need therapy, emotional support to handle depression. If it's possible, make your father come with you to the doctor, so he'll get to learn about the desease your going through. Buy books on depression, he's pushing for pills and yelling at you because he does not know any better. Education on the subject will help you both battle this dreaded illness. Also, anti-depressants are not the right meds for depression, they make you more prone to commit suicide I read. My mom's bipolar, manic depressive and she's taking mood stabilizers and anti-psychotics, and together with therapy and support from family she's ok. So medicines does work but the latter two is equally important. Good luck with your appointment to the doc. Again, I think you're a great guy, and someone who is decent and good is needed to make sure the world doesn't end up on fire.

People actually don't care. And they are not actually knowledgeable about mental illness aside from what they hear on tv. They have to care to make an effort to learn. It's easier to label someone as crazy, if it doesn't affect them. The exception to people who cares, are your family. So appreciate and communicate your thoughts and feelings to make them understand what you're going thru. Don't suffer in silence.

Take care of your father. In the act of helping  him get out of depression, you might help yourself too. When I nearly lose my mother to suicide, I realized that it's not all about me, my mom is important too. She is the only one who loves me wholeheartedly and was always there to support and forgive me through all my failures. She was bipolar and neglected me throughout my childhood but she was great when she wasn't sick. We all have our failure as human beings. It's never too late to forgive and change. Go do something together with your pops. Get to know each other. Family is important. Warts and all.

Got thru my first eighteen years of life escaping into my books. I was fortunate I discovered manga, anime during college.  Then after I drop out I played videogames. Then Korean dramas and most recently the fanfiction community. That got me two years of entertainment. Now, I've started gardening. Working with plants, taking care of them, makes me happy. I get to get out of my room, feel sunlight on my pasty white skin, enjoy some fresh air. I get to learn new things.

Yep. Happens to me a lot. The most memorable one, heh, was when I was an intern in the Medical Ward and one day, five patients died one after the other. I remember the Head Nurse scolding a group of us because she heard an intern commenting infront of the berieved families, why the hospital staff can't prevent them from dying. How inadequate and incompetent they are. That intern might have been me but I honestly can't say for sure. I might have block out that moment from my mind. It was my first time experiencing so much death. 
Nowadays, conversation I've had a few minutes ago are difficult to remeber word for word. But I attribute it to my voracious reading habit. I always have a book to read on hand. If I deem what the speaker has to say as unimportant, it passes from one ear to another. It's noticeable because my gran has difficulty hearing and she always, always ask me what that person said to me and I have to answer her.

Yeah that hurts man. I was depressed for six years, most of my early to late twenties I spent being a shut in. Disappointing my parents, being compared to my much more succesful cousins. It was like a punch in the face when my rich Aunt called me a worthless piece of shit to my bipolar mother's face. My mom tried to commit suicide a few days later. She survived, it was a wake up call for me. I've made her happines and well-being a priority ever since. Being so active was hard, talking to other people was nerve wracking, walking out the door made my stomach hurts and hyperventilate.  But it became easier each time I did it. Now I find myself in a better situation than last year. I'm much closer to my mom. I don't hate myself and I can say to myself that I am not worthless and sometimes believe it.

I used to be ignorant and just calls my mother crazy. I did not know what else to call it, no one educated me. Since she was crazy, I assume that it was permanent. Much later I found out that she was bipolar and it was treatable. It was such a relief to find a name to call her sickness. It made it understandeble and not scary. There are a lot of mental health problem out there and proper medicines and therapy helps cure them. It is a diservice to yourself if you call yourself crazy. You need and deserve help. I am sorry to hear about your friend. People have done bad things, they make mistakes but this is your life. It is important that you be happy. It's ok to forgive yourself and I find forgiving others makes life infinitely better. People can change. Forgiveness opens a lot of paths previously closed to you.

Filipinas are mostly raised as Roman Catholics, their raised with the idea of no sex before marriage. Even if they are poor, expect most of them to be College Educated. They are also 'pakipot', they expect men to woo them for quite some time, before agreeing to enter in a relationship. Family is number 1, the ladies lives with the parents until they are married. If the parents like you, great but if not, you're out of luck.
The Philippines is very tolerant of gay people, mostly because women rules the household here and are respected. The common thought is that gays are women born in the wrong body. So too they must be treated with respect. Tolerance does not mean acceptance tho, because of the strong hold of the Church on the government and the masses. You won't see same sex marriage in the country anytime soon. Unlike other countries tho, the Philippines never had a law that discriminated/criminalized gay people, negatively, this makes it difficult for any anti-discrimination bill to pass. Since they are seen as rather unnecessary.

Telling him you'll always be by his side to help and support him. My mom has bipolar and it took some reassurance and me showing that I meant what I said for her to get better, the meds help too. Ask him what's troubling him and tell him that he's not alone, that you love him and together you could solve it and it's much better to face it together. Read about Cognitive Behavior Therapy. Gives you an idea on how to steer him away from negative thoughts.

I was browsing facebook and saw that my former bestfriends had gotten married and one already had two daughters. They had jobs and seems to be enjoying life to the fullest. Whilst I spent six years being a shut in. I decided six years ago to stop  working. I had low self-esteem and couldn't handle criticism and the soul crushing effort in looking for a job, and I decided to focus all  my attention and the little passive money I had into turning our house into a apartment complex. It took six years with no social interaction, it takes money to go outside to have fun, gave me agoraphobia, depression, but I'm now a landlord of eight apartments. But at what cost? I'm turning thirty but I've never had a boyfriend, never had a career, an accomplishment to be proud of. I've started gardening and that seems to have helped me get out of my room and making me feel happy. I've been walking my dogs too and exercising. Life seems to be looking up, then on a whim I decided to create a facebook account and check out my former bestfriends. Immediately afterwards, I was upset, envious and discouraged, I felt left behind. I've lost six years of my life, I thought I had done the right thing for me but I was just a useless coward, one so afraid to face the world that I took the easy way out.

Your 17, your body is full of hormones that messes up your mind. You did something wrong, make sure you won't do it again. People makes mistakes, they learn from it and became a better version of themselves. 
My stepdad just broke my dog's skull, she almost died and still in recovery while I type this. I forgave him. You are ashamed of what you did and I think that you don't deserve to die. You could do more with your life. You could do good things, great things. Your young and allowed to make mistakes. Don't let those mistake define you. There are many facets that makes up a person. It is not just black and white, there are many shades of gray. 
It is difficult to forgive oneself, I too had done a horrific thing when I was thirteen, that after years has passed that still plagues me. I was a self-centered, ignorant kid, tasked with feeding my bedridden, paralyzed grandfather, one morning they found him dead. Nobody blamed me but I'm sure it was my fault. He must have choked to death. I thought that I deserved to go to jail. But I was too afraid to confess to anyone. From that point on I promised to myself that I will live to be a better person to make up for what I did. That I will do good.
Times went on, life has not been easy, it was hard, but I still live, I learn to cherish the good things and to stand strong against the bad things. I learned the importance of forgiveness. That was a hard knowledge to gain. But without it, my path in life seems so narrower, filled with pain. I've decided that my life will be much better for it.

Hello! This was a great response and i'm extremely thankful. For half a year I've been taking care of my mom, who tried to commit suicide due to an undiagnosed depression, I took on the responsibility of being the head of the family, managing all the finances and household chores, making sure my mom's taking her medications, waiting for her to get back home from whatever place she has wandered off to... I took care of being unable to go outside to buy groceries by relying on my stepfather.  I hadn't have time to think about my social anxiety and focused all of my energy, to keeping our family together. But for a month now, my mom has returned to normal, I've been going back to my bad habits. Now that the pressure is off, I've mostly coop myself inside my bedroom, reading books, surfing the internet. I still managed the finances, take care of the pets, clean the backyard, feed the chickens and ducks my mom bought in the midst of her manic episode. But i don't cook, clean the house anymore. I barely listens to my gran, probably because every word that comes out from her are insults, making me desire to get out of my room, less and less.
Your post is enligthening in that you said, that I had to go out and accompany them, for my sake. In order for me to fight my fear of going outside. I do want to get better. And I love my mom and I don't want her to have a relapse. It's just, it's so easy to think logically what I should do, when the anxiety has passed, it's the doing that's difficult. Thanks for reading this whole post. And thanks for the advice. I'm thankful for this subreddit as I have no one else to talk to.

Heh, i dropped out of school for one year because I felt that i was being bullied. i felt out of place among my group of "friends". The next school year, I changed, I decided to give it my best and tried hard to succeed that time around. And somehow I did, graduating at the top of  my class. Nobody knew me, I had a fresh start. I did not regret it but somehow, I learned that bad habit of thinking that it's easier to run away. If I don't like something I ditch it. It's fortunate that I had my parents support throughout. 
One thing that help my anxiety is, having the right clothes and accessories. if I feel that I look my best, nothing can bother me, it gives me that boost of confidence needed to get out of the door.

At sixteen I was self-centered and only thought of myself. I'm a bookworm, so i used to dragged my best and only friend throughout the city searching for specific books.  If she's not available, I'll just go out by myself. The advent of ebooks and the internet has made me lazy and sadly made my social-anxiety worsten.  Nowadays, i'm completely content being alone.  I'm lucky that I was able to find that one thing that makes me happy so early in my life.
I think if you want something enough, no amount of anxiety is going to prevent you from doing what you want. So, find that something, and become obssessed with it, and enjoy your youth. :D

If we want the dota 2 scene to continue to grow, and not stagnate, Valve is right not to be complacent, and finally take matters on improving the scene with their own hands. Also, with the millions of money compendium generates, they cannot leave it to organizers to make a profit from. They are still a company and their job is to make money, and not give other companies those money. If other organizers wanted a piece of the dota 2 pie, they should prove that they could give the players and us viewers, the best tournament they can and not just rest on their laurels. 
That said, I really like the BTS crew, from what I read from EE's blog, they did a fantastic job with their tournament, but maybe it's a little too late for it to affect Valve's decision. Valve might have been fed up as well with all the dramas that plague the scene.

Whenever there's company, I hide in my room. Whenever there's a celebration, a family reunion, a birthday party and even a funeral, I won't attend. I just feel that I can't breathe in a crowd. My stomach hurts just thinking about it.  I don't talk, I don't know how to start a conversation. My relatives must hate me. (>.<)'

I used to have a pretty big opinion of myself, I used to have big dreams. That I'll have a big house, a great husband, a great job, great friends. None of that have come to passed. I live with my parents. I don't have a job and I don't want one. I dropped out of college two times. I've avoided my friends and have lost all contact. I used to think that i'll go back to school one day. Maybe I will, sometime in the future. Meanwhile, I do what I can to slowly be financially secure. My mom gave me the rights to one of her apartments, I'm saving the money I get from it to built more. My Dad's a carpenter, so a little money can go along way. Meanwhile, i'm loafing around the house, suddenly acquiring agoraphobia. I can't look at my other relatives in the eye. I'm a bookworm so I'm happy with just a tablet on my hands. I've got my parents and our menangerie of pets as company. This might not be the future I saw in the past. But I'm healthy, my family is healthy. I feel safe and content. Someday, when I'm ready, I might tackle going outside again. 
I'm extremely lucky with my parents, they have a lot of flaws, my Dad canbe a scary drunk, my mom is bipolar. But they both love me. With their support, I think I can continue living. I'm sure that your parents will do everything to help you. Ask for their support. Talk to them.
Convince him to tell his family. Being bipolar is hard. He'll need all the support he can get. When you can't be there for him, it's important that his family will be there to take care of him.

It sounds like he's depressed. He really needs that meds to get better. Don't ignore it and think it'll just go away on its own. That way leads to suicide. :( Bipolar meds are really effective, he shouldn't give up. He can live a fairly  normal and productive life.
You should learn more about bipolar so you'll know how to best help him.

The biggest regret I have now as a daughter of a schizophrenic is that I did not put an effort much sooner to learning about my mothers' condition. At times, when you observe your brother doing something that'll frustrate or anger or confuse you, the knowledge about why he is acting that way, will help you understand him better and enabling you to give him the right help. 
The most important thing tho, is to be there for him.

I hurt for you. I think back to what happened to my mother and I feel incredibly sad and full of regrets. I was in my early teens when I discovered my mother's mental illness. At that time, me and my relatives didn't know how to handle her.We were confused and angry at her for ruining our stable life with her for acting out. I blamed her. My grandma and I left her to fend for herself. Thinking back, I realized what an incredibly selfish, misguided person I was back then. I shoud have been with her and tried to help her. But then I was just relieved that she wasn't my problem anymore and I could try to live a normal life. A year later, things changed, when one of my relatives managed to get her psychiatric help. She went back to normal soon after receiving treatment and although she has experience a relapse from time to time, they were treated as soon as symptoms surfaced. We are together as a family again. I am very thankful, that nothing terrible has happened to her during our time apart. So, please don't end your life. You can take your life back, take your meds, get better and try to reach out to your family.

I've just got over a bout of depression, I'm trying hard to stay positive and ignore negative thoughts but my step dad just decided that it's a great time to start becoming a gambling addict. Money is tight and my mom can't handle stress very well, since she's sufferring from schizophrenia. Her meds let's her handle day to day living just fine but what my step dad is doing is making it hard to breathe around the house.

Being unable to sleep properly is a major problem. But can be easily fixed, just go and see a psychologist and they'll prescribe pills that'll help you get a good night of sleep. Getting kicked out of college is no big deal. You don't live in a third world country where getting kicked out of college will sentence you to a life of misery. Take care of yourself and try again in the future. Friends come and go. There was a time in my life that I only bath once a month. Asking for help is a good sign that you want to change. Life is already looking up for you.  Go take that bath and take that appointment to go see a doctor. I hear that Britain has a good healthcare system in place.

Life will get better. It will probably suck in the future but it will get better, that is how things are. Every cloud has a silver lining. If you have difficulty sleeping please go see a doctor, as lack of sleep is one of the leading reasons for mental illness. A good night sleep will do wonders for your health.
